exact_current_claim.sampling_basis: All 12 occurrences are a single fully-lexicalized noun (عَصَا / عِصِيّ, pos_tag N throughout) and every attestation sits inside the Moses/magicians narrative cycle (Ṭā Hā 20, Shuʿarāʿ 26, Naml 27, Qaṣaṣ 28, Aʿrāf 7, Baqara 2). The packet contains no verbal, participial, or abstract derivation of the root. The invariant is therefore complete and STRONG for THIS lexeme, but the sample cannot license a UNIVERSAL claim about the whole root's semantics: it is one lexeme in one narrative genre, so scope is capped at REPRESENTATIVE.
exact_current_claim.preferred_conclusion: Across all 12 occurrences the root ع ص و contributes exactly one concrete count noun: عَصَا (sg.) / عِصِيّ (pl.) = a rigid, elongated, hand-held rod/staff. The referent is internally fixed by 20:18:3:1, where Moses defines it by ordinary uses (leaning upon it أَتَوَكَّؤُا, beating down foliage for his flock أَهُشُّ, and other purposes). Every other occurrence is consistent with this same physical object: it is cast down (object of أَلْقِ/أَلْقَىٰ at 26:32, 26:45, 27:10, 28:31, 7:107, 7:117, and pl. 26:44), or used to strike a target (اضْرِب بِعَصَاكَ at 26:63, 2:60, 7:160), or held generically by the magicians (pl. عِصِيّ at 20:66, 26:44). The root supplies ONLY the physical-implement concept 'staff'; all miraculous transformations and effects are supplied by the governing verbs and narrative frame, not by the root.
exact_current_claim.root_concept: A rigid, elongated, hand-held rod/staff — the concrete count noun عَصَا / عِصِيّ (grasped, leaned upon, cast, or struck-with).
exact_current_claim.plain_explanation: In these 12 verses the root always means a physical walking-stick/rod that a person holds. Verse 20:18 spells out its plain uses (Moses leans on it and knocks down leaves for his sheep). Elsewhere it is thrown down or used to hit the sea or a rock. The dramatic results (it turns into a snake, swallows the magicians' tricks, splits the sea, brings out water) come from what the verse says happens to the staff, not from the word 'staff' itself. The magicians also have 'staffs' (plural), which shows the word is just an ordinary object, not something magical or unique to Moses.
exact_current_claim.semantic_boundary: The sense is bounded as a RIGID rod, explicitly contrasted with flexible rope: عِصِيّ is coordinated with but distinct from حِبَال ('ropes') at 20:66:6:2 and 26:44:3:2. It is an ORDINARY physical tool (fixed by the mundane use-list at 20:18:3:1), not an inherently miraculous or Moses-specific item (the magicians own a plural set). It excludes any abstract, verbal, or figurative value — none is attested. It also excludes the near-homograph root ع ص ي (disobedience, final radical yāʿ), which is a different root and contributes nothing here.

layer_attribution.derivation: Only inflectional/number morphology: singular عَصَا with possessive suffixes (-ya 20:18, -hu 26:32/26:45/7:107, -ka 26:63/27:10/28:31/2:60/7:117/7:160) vs. broken plural عِصِيّ (20:66, 26:44). Number and person do not split the sense.

layer_attribution.context: Narrative frame supplies all extraordinary outcomes external to the root: transformation into serpent (26:32, 7:107) or quivering snake (27:10, 28:31), swallowing the illusions (26:45, 7:117), splitting the sea (26:63), gushing springs from rock (2:60, 7:160), and the magicians' illusion of motion (20:66).

exact_current_claim.sampling_basis: The nucleus is induced from the productive, confounder-free minority (~20 tokens) that spans four independent form-classes and both spatial and scalar frames, NOT from the bleached majority. Concrete verbs/participles (6): 53:8, 33:59:8, 55:54, 69:23, 76:14, 6:99. Spatial elatives fixed by overt in-verse contrast (6): 8:42 (dunyaa vs quSwaa), 37:6 / 41:12 / 67:5 (nearest heaven), 30:3, 53:9. Scalar elatives with numeric/degree antonyms (3): 32:21 (adnaa vs akbar), 58:7 (adnaa vs akthar), 73:20 (less than two-thirds). Elative↔dunyaa bridge (1): 7:169 (عرض هذا الأدنى parallel to متاع الدنيا). The remaining ~110 tokens are the lexicalized ٱلْحَيَوٰة ٱلدُّنْيَا / ٱلدُّنْيَا-as-substantive mass (e.g. 10:23, 47:36, 57:20, 2:114, 3:22), where the root is bleached; they are treated as confirmations of the etymon but NOT as the sampling base, to avoid circularity. Scope is REPRESENTATIVE rather than UNIVERSAL precisely because the generalization is soundly established on this cross-cutting sample and holds as the root's etymological contribution everywhere, but is NOT the live clause-level meaning of the dominant lexicalized mass.
exact_current_claim.preferred_conclusion: The root د ن و contributes a single coherent nucleus: NEARNESS / PROXIMITY — "near, close, low, within reach" — whose elative (أدنى) projects onto non-spatial scales as "lower / lesser / fewer." This invariant is directly demonstrated by four independent, internally-bridged form-classes in the packet: the finite verb of physical approach دَنَا (53:8:2:1 دَنَا فَتَدَلَّىٰ), the form-IV يُدْنِينَ "draw/lower [garments]" (33:59:8:1), the participle دَانٍ/دَانِيَة for fruit and shade that is close/low-hanging/reachable (55:54:9:1, 69:23:2:1, 76:14:1:2, 6:99:24:1), and the spatial elative fixed by overt in-packet contrast — ٱلْعُدْوَة ٱلدُّنْيَا "the NEARER bank" opposed to ٱلْقُصْوَىٰ "the farther" (8:42:4:2), ٱلسَّمَآء ٱلدُّنْيَا "the nearest heaven" (37:6, 41:12, 67:5), أَدْنَى ٱلْأَرْضِ (30:3), أَوْ أَدْنَىٰ (53:9). No occurrence contradicts "near/low." However, the root's contribution is the ONLY thing it supplies; three other layers are demonstrably NOT the root: (a) the heavily lexicalized feminine elative ٱلدُّنْيَا / ٱلْحَيَوٰة ٱلدُّنْيَا = "the present world/life" (~110 of 133 tokens), where the "world" sense is minted by the fixed collocation plus the ٱلْـَٔاخِرَة antithesis, not freshly by the root — the root there is bleached to an inert "nearer (life)"; (b) the modal "more apt/likely/conducive" reading, supplied by the أَدْنَىٰ + أَن construction (4:3:26:1, 2:282:93:2, 5:108:2:1, 33:51:17:1, 33:59:13:1); (c) the "worldly/transient/deceptive" connotations, supplied by predicates (لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ، مَتَٰعُ ٱلْغُرُورِ، زِينَة), not by د ن و. So the nucleus generalizes across the root as its etymological contribution, but is the LIVE clause-level meaning only in the productive minority.
exact_current_claim.root_concept: NEARNESS / PROXIMITY (spatial: near, close, low, within reach), elative projecting to LOWER / LESSER / FEWER
exact_current_claim.plain_explanation: The root د ن و means "to be near / close / low / within reach." You can see it plainly where fruit hangs low and reachable (55:54, 69:23, 76:14, 6:99), where someone "drew near" (53:8), and where "the nearer bank" is set against "the farther bank" (8:42) and "the nearest heaven" is named (37:6, 41:12, 67:5). Its comparative form أدنى then stretches naturally to "lower / lesser / fewer" on any scale (fewer than that, 58:7; less than two-thirds of the night, 73:20; the lesser punishment vs the greater, 32:21). Two things that look like the root's meaning are actually added by grammar and habit, not by the root: the phrase "أدنى + that..." meaning "more likely/fitting" (the أن-clause does that work), and the fixed word الدنيا = "this present world" (its "world" meaning comes from always being paired with "life" and contrasted with "the Hereafter"). Because that fixed "this world" word is the overwhelming majority of uses and its "nearness" flavor is worn away, we affirm the nucleus strongly for the productive family but stop short of claiming it is the operative meaning everywhere.
exact_current_claim.semantic_boundary: IN (the root's own contribution): spatial proximity/closeness, low position, reachability (دَنَا, يُدْنِينَ, دَانٍ/دَانِيَة); and the elative projection of "near/low" onto degree/quantity scales — "nearer, lower, lesser, fewer" (أدنى: 30:3, 8:42, 53:9, 32:21, 58:7, 73:20). OUT (supplied by other layers, must not be loaded onto the root): the substantive "this present world/life" (lexicalization of ٱلدُّنْيَا + collocation with ٱلْحَيَوٰة + antithesis to ٱلْـَٔاخِرَة); the modal "more apt/likely/conducive" (the أَدْنَىٰ + أَن construction); and evaluative "worldly/vain/deceptive/transient" (the predicates لعب/لهو/غرور/زينة/متاع). BORDERLINE: the value sense "inferior/meaner" in 2:61 (أدنى opposed to خير) — reachable from the root only via "low end of a scale" (parallel to 32:21 الأدنى↔الأكبر), but on packet evidence alone it cannot be excluded that this token belongs to a homophonous root of baseness folded under dnw; it is written identically (أدنى), so no in-packet morphology discriminates it.

exact_current_claim.strongest_counterexample: 2:61:27:1 — ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ set directly against ٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ: the discriminating antonym is quality/value ("inferior/meaner"), not distance or height. A purely spatial-nearness nucleus reaches this only by the inferential leap near→low→base, and the token cannot be excluded (from packet evidence alone) from a homophonous baseness root d-n-' folded under dnw. It does not overturn the nucleus (the low-end-of-scale reading is continuous with 32:21 الأدنى↔الأكبر), but it is where the nucleus is least directly demonstrated. The complementary scope-limiting counterexample is the ~110-token lexicalized ٱلْحَيَوٰة ٱلدُّنْيَا mass (e.g. 47:36:3:2, 57:20:4:2) where nearness is synchronically inert and the operative meaning is supplied by the ٱلْـَٔاخِرَة antithesis.

exact_current_claim.preferred_conclusion: Within the Form IV family (أَفْلَحَ / يُفْلِحُ / تُفْلِحُونَ and the active participle ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ), which is the ONLY form attested across all 40 occurrences, ف ل ح contributes a single valence-neutral nucleus: "to attain the desired favorable terminal outcome — to succeed, prosper, thrive, come out ahead." The finite verb asserts, denies, or hopes for that outcome for a stated class of persons; the participle names the party that attains it. The predicate is polar and the same abstract notion is applied with opposite polarity to good and bad referents: affirmed of the righteous/prevailing (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ 23:1; قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ 87:14; قَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ 20:64) and denied of wrongdoer classes (لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ 10:17; ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ 12:23, 28:37, 6:21, 6:135; ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ 23:117, 28:82; ٱلسَّاحِرُونَ/ٱلسَّاحِرُ 10:77, 20:69; fabricators 10:69, 16:116). exact_current_claim.root_concept: Attain the desired favorable outcome; succeed, prosper, thrive, come out ahead (Form IV attainment predicate).
exact_current_claim.plain_explanation: Every one of the 40 places uses one Arabic verb-shape (Form IV): either the verb "aflaḥa/yufliḥu" (succeed/come out well) or its doer-noun "al-mufliḥūn" (the successful ones). The shared meaning is simply "to attain the good outcome one is after." The Qurʾan uses it like a scoreboard: it is DENIED to wrongdoers, liars, sorcerers, disbelievers, and oppressors, and AFFIRMED (or hoped for) of believers, the God-fearing, and those who purify themselves. Crucially, the same word is used for a purely worldly win — Pharaoh's magicians say "whoever prevails today has aflaḥa" (20:64) — so the word itself does not mean "salvation." When the meaning looks religious, that comes from the surrounding words (e.g., "who purifies himself" in 87:14), not from ف ل ح. exact_current_claim.preferred_conclusion: The root ف و ه contributes a single concrete anatomical concept: the mouth, i.e. the body's oral aperture. It is attested exclusively as one lexicalized noun (فاه singular at 13:14:18:1; أفواه plural in the other 12), POS=N throughout. Three purely physical uses fix the sense as the concrete organ with no speech content: water reaching the mouth (13:14:18:1), hands thrust into mouths (14:9:24:1), and mouths sealed shut (36:65:4:1). In the remaining occurrences the organ serves as the source of egress in the min-ablative frame (word issuing from mouths 18:5:12:1; hatred appearing from mouths 3:118:19:1) or as the instrument of utterance in the bi-instrumental frame (24:15:5:2, 33:4:22:2, 3:167:25:2, 5:41:13:2, 9:30:13:2, 9:8:12:2, 61:8:5:2, 9:32:6:2). In every case the speech, insincerity, and futility content is supplied by the verb (قول/تخرج/بدت/يطفئوا/نختم) and the construction (bi-, min-, and the قلوب/صدور/نور contrast), while the root itself supplies only the physical organ. The bare-organ reading substitutes in all 13 occurrences without exception.
exact_current_claim.plain_explanation: Across all 13 Quranic occurrences this root just means "mouth" — the physical opening of the body. It never appears as a verb or any other derived form; it is always the same noun (singular فاه, plural أفواه). We know the meaning is the concrete organ, not "speech," because three verses use it with no talking at all: water trying to reach a man's mouth, people putting their hands to their mouths, and God sealing mouths shut. In the verses about hypocrites "saying with their mouths what is not in their hearts," the idea of insincere or empty talk comes from the words "say," the little word "with," and the contrast with "hearts" — not from the root itself, which still only names the mouth.
exact_current_claim.semantic_boundary: The root's contribution stops at the physical oral aperture (mouth). It does NOT itself encode: (a) speech/utterance as an abstraction — that comes from verbs of saying and the min-/bi- frames; (b) insincerity or lip-service — that comes from the explicit mouth-vs-heart/breast contrast (قلوب/صدور); (c) futility of opposition — that comes from the "extinguish the light" metaphor (يطفئوا نور الله) in 61:8/9:32. The singular/plural alternation (فاه vs أفواه) is a number/inflection matter, not a semantic split. There is no attested verbal, participial, adjectival, or maṣdar derivation in this corpus, so no productive root-level abstraction is licensed.

layer_attribution.root: mouth = the physical oral aperture of the body (invariant across all 13 occurrences)

exact_current_claim.plain_explanation: In every one of its 13 Quranic occurrences the word ghulām means a young male person — a boy or youth. That is all the word itself pins down: he is male, and he is not (yet) a grown adult. Everything else the stories add — that he is a promised son (Yahyā to Zakariyyā 19:7; the child announced to Mary 19:19; the son promised to Abraham 15:53, 37:101, 51:28), a foundling sold as merchandise (Joseph 12:19), an innocent who is slain (18:74), two inheriting orphans (18:82), or serving youths in Paradise (52:24) — comes from the surrounding words and grammar, not from ghulām. We can prove this: where the word carries no possessive or gift construction (52:24 servers who belong-to but are not born-to the blessed; 12:19 Joseph, unrelated to his finders) there is no 'son' meaning at all, so 'son' lives in the construction, not the root. The maleness is real and constant (a son, not a daughter, is the gift in 19:19; no female ghulām occurs anywhere), and youth is real and constant (orphans not yet mature 18:82; the pearl-like lads 52:24). But the exact age is loose — it stretches from a not-yet-conceived promised child (3:40, 19:8) to a boy old enough to be feared for future rebellion (18:80) — so the word fixes 'young male,' not any tight age.
exact_current_claim.semantic_boundary: INSIDE the root/lexeme's contribution: [+male] (human) and [+young/pre-full-adult].
